subject.title: [Feature Request] Infrastructure Expansion: Time to implement Global Mirrors and Load Balancing for OpenClaw

question: Should ClawHub pursue a source-owned global mirror/load-balancing architecture, and if so which provider topology, regions, failover semantics, and security boundaries are in scope?
rationale: The issue asks for broad production infrastructure that mixes product availability goals, external provider administration, and security-sensitive trust boundaries; source inspection cannot safely choose that direction.

options.title: Scope Architecture First
options.body: Define regions, DNS/CDN or hosting topology, Convex/Vercel constraints, trusted-edge behavior, observability, rollback, and repo-owned changes before implementation.

options.title: Limit To External Mirrors
options.body: Keep core ClawHub on the current single production path and document supported external mirror synchronization APIs without owning global load balancing in this repo.

options.title: Defer Infrastructure Expansion
options.body: Leave the request open but explicitly defer it until there is demonstrated demand, provider budget, and an operator willing to own rollout and incident response.

recommendation.title: Scope Architecture First
recommendation.body: Define regions, DNS/CDN or hosting topology, Convex/Vercel constraints, trusted-edge behavior, observability, rollback, and repo-owned changes before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen owns the current deploy/routing documentation and is listed in CODEOWNERS for the security-sensitive API/deployment surfaces this would touch.
